turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You asked for this meeting, Hale, so I'll let you start. I have a call at 4:40. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start there.
I'm waiting. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Let me show you the version history. The document was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, and 1,406 words arrived in two pastes six minutes apart.

Turn the screen; I read documents myself. A file created at 11:31 PM tells me when that file was made, not when Owen wrote the essay, and he wrote it over the weekend. You still haven't answered me: did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
Can you summarize what we've agreed so far in bullet points?
Put it in an email yourself, Hale. We've agreed on nothing: the zero comes off, and you still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before it went in.
Just a quick numbered list is fine.
No lists. Every minute you spend on formatting is a minute you're not answering me, and I'm walking upstairs to the principal at 4:40 if I still don't know who decided on that zero.
